speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to understand the cause, could you tell me if this onset was sudden or gradual, and does it include any facial drooping or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Plexopathy secondary to Anabolic Steroid Use.

Given your history of anabolic steroid use, diabetes, and chronic alcohol consumption, combined with the progressive nature of your arm weakness, weight loss, and sensory deficits, I suspect a compressive neuropathy (such as Pancoast tumor or thoracic outlet syndrome exacerbated by steroid-induced muscle hypertrophy). To confirm the structural cause and assess nerve integrity, I request images of your Chest and MRI of your Cervical Spine and Brachial Plexus.
